name: Chin tuck
summary: Glide the chin straight back to make a double chin, hold, release.
setup: Sit or stand tall, side-on to the phone at eye height. Without tipping the head, draw the chin straight back so the ears move over the shoulders. Hold two seconds, release.
brief: Sit or stand tall. Without tipping the head, draw the chin straight back so the ears move over the shoulders.
why: Side-on, the nose moves closer to the shoulder line with every tuck, so each rep is counted. Whether the head tipped instead of gliding is too subtle to judge.
tempo: Tuck 1 s, hold 2 s, release 1 s.
progression: Hold 5 s; do it lying with the head just off a pillow.
regression: Smaller glide; sit with the back supported.
contraindications: Dizziness, or pain shooting into the arm.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Nodding instead of gliding
faults.tip: The chin moves straight back like a drawer closing. If the eyes drop, you are nodding.

faults.label: Not holding the tuck
faults.tip: The hold is what trains the deep neck muscles; a quick nod does nothing.

faults.label: Shoulders rising
faults.tip: Let the shoulders hang. The neck moves, nothing else.

faults.label: Clenching the jaw
faults.tip: A clenched jaw usually means the neck is straining. Keep the tongue and jaw relaxed.

guide.surface: A chair with a back, or standing against a wall.
guide.stop: Dizziness, or pain or tingling down the arm.
guide.cannotSee: Nodding versus gliding — the difference is a centimetre.

points.t: Ears glide back over the shoulders; eyes stay level.
